description:
FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 1).  t/re/pat.t is DIFF 231/138 with
ONE aborted top-level form whose message is the FILE'S OWN die:

    aborted-forms:1: Failed to match at pat.t line N.

so 898 of perl's 1,267 rows are never produced -- the single biggest remaining
`re/` shortfall outside the registered classes.

WHAT IS KNOWN: the message comes from pat.t itself, not from PCL, i.e. one of
the file's guarded assertions (`... or die "Failed to match at pat.t line " .
__LINE__`) failed and took the rest of the top-level form with it.  The row
count says the stop is around perl row 370.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, and is the first job: WHICH line.  `PCL_SUITE_KEEP=DIR
tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 re/pat.t` keeps `<DIR>/re_pat.t.out`; the
recovery line there carries the real line number (the runner normalises digits
to N in the `sig` column, which is why the blessed text reads "line N").  Then
read that assertion and probe it alone -- it is one regex, and the 898 rows
behind it make it worth a session on its own.

DO NOT assume the 898 rows all share the cause: the s473t5a rule is that a
recovery line proves an abort, never that the abort cost the rows that follow
it.  pat.t's 138 blessed fail rows are a separate, scattered population (the
file is perl's own regex grab-bag).
subject: t/re/pat.t dies at its own `Failed to match at pat.t line N` and loses 898 of 1,267 rows -- the abort is ONE assertion inside an `ok(...) or die` guard
